keyboard.cap: Keyboard fires when a key is pressed (down), released (up) or held. Set “Key” to the key you want – here Space.

collision.cap: Collision fires when this object touches another – set “With” to a tag or name. Here the box slides into a wall.

mouseMove.cap: Mouse Move sends the pointer position as it moves. Feed it into Position (source: signalXY) and the box follows the mouse.

always.cap: Always runs every frame while it is enabled. Here it feeds a Spin block, so the box turns without any input.

timer.cap: Timer sends a signal every “interval” seconds (here 0.8 s). Wire it to anything that should repeat.

once.cap: Once fires a single time – when the scene starts (or after a delay). Perfect for setting things up.

mouseClick.cap: Mouse Click fires when the mouse button is clicked – anywhere, or only on this object (set “On” to self). It also sends the click position.

mouseWheel.cap: Mouse Wheel sends “up” or “down” when you scroll. Here scrolling up grows the box and down shrinks it.

gesture.cap: Gesture recognises a swipe, tap, double tap or pinch with mouse or finger. A swipe left pushes the box left.

lockedMouse.cap: Locked Mouse captures the mouse (click the game) and sends how far it moved (dx, dy) – the basis of mouse-look in first-person games.

controller.cap: Controller listens to a gamepad button or stick (here button 0 = A / Cross). Plug in a pad and press it.

inView.cap: In View fires when the object enters or leaves the camera view. Here the box slides off the right edge.

sensor.cap: Sensor watches any value – a position, a variable – and fires when it crosses a limit. Here: when x is greater than 650.

mailbox.cap: Mailbox receives messages sent by a Message block (here on the channel “hello”), from any object or scene.

custom.cap: Custom Trigger runs your own JavaScript: call fire(value) whenever you want to send a signal. Here it fires every 0.8 s.

number.cap: Number outputs a fixed value whenever a signal arrives. Use it to turn “something happened” into a number.

expression.cap: Expression calculates a formula from its inputs a, b, c … Here a * 2 + 1 with a = 5 gives 11.

customBehavior.cap: Custom Block runs your own JavaScript on every incoming signal; “value” is the signal, return the answer. Here it squares 4.

globalVariable.cap: Global Variable stores a value any object can read. Each Space press adds 1 to “score”; its out port sends the new value.

objectVariable.cap: Object Variable is a value that belongs to one object (like “health”). Each press subtracts 10 from this box’s health.

ease.cap: Ease turns “start” into a smooth 0 → 1 curve (here quadOut over 1 s). Wired to Alpha, the box fades smoothly instead of jumping.

repeater.cap: Repeater turns one signal into several (count 4, every 0.3 s) – handy for bursts, volleys or retries.

random.cap: Random sends a random number (here 0–100, whole numbers) or makes a chance decision. Press Space for a new value.

filter.cap: Filter lets a signal through only if it passes a test. Here only random numbers above 50 get through to “pass”.

switch.cap: Switch is a gate: signals pass only while it is on. A turns it off, S turns it on – Space only works while it is on.

toggleSwitch.cap: Toggle Switch alternates between its two outputs each time it gets “next”: out1 turns the box red, out2 blue.

caseSwitch.cap: Case Switch sends the signal out of the output whose name matches the value (cases “a, b, c”). Here “b” takes the middle path.

router.cap: Router sends a signal to one of several outputs – here round-robin: each press goes to the next colour.

logicGate.cap: Logic Gate combines two true/false inputs. With AND, the “true” output fires only when both A and B were pressed.

sound.cap: Sound plays a sound (or stops / mutes it). Add sounds in the Assets tab; here the box pulses while it plays.

emit.cap: Emit Particles shoots a burst of particles (colour, speed, spread, life…). Press Space for a burst from the box.

spawn.cap: Spawn creates copies of a template object (here “Coin”). Each press spawns one that flies up.

attacher.cap: Attach glues another object to this one so they move together. Press Space to attach the ball, then the box carries it away.

physics.cap: Physics gives an object a body: gravity, bounce, friction, collisions. Press Space to make the box dynamic – it falls and bounces.

joint.cap: Joint ties this object to an anchor like a rope or spring (distance + stiffness). Press Space to hang the box from the anchor – it swings.

proximity.cap: Proximity fires when another object comes within a radius (here 150 px of the player). Great for doors, enemies and pick-ups.

pushMotor.cap: Push Motor keeps pushing an object in a direction (speed or acceleration). Press Space to start the engine.

spinMotor.cap: Spin Motor turns an object continuously (degrees per second). With “autoStart” it spins from the moment the game starts.

impulse.cap: Impulse gives an object a sudden push – the classic jump. Press Space to kick the box upward.

pointAt.cap: Point At turns an object to face a target – here the mouse. Move the pointer and the arrow follows.

enabled.cap: Enabled switches an object on or off (hidden, no physics, no logic). Space toggles the other box on and off.

material.cap: Material changes how a 3D object looks: colour, metalness, roughness, glow, texture, opacity. Space turns the sphere shiny red.

flip.cap: Flip mirrors an object horizontally and/or vertically. The arrow flips left ↔ right with each Space press.

extractor.cap: Extractor reads a property of an object (x, y, angle, size…) and sends it out. Press Space to read the box’s x.

displayOrder.cap: Display Order decides which object is drawn in front. Press Space to bring the blue box in front of the red one.

blending.cap: Blending changes how colours mix with what is behind: normal, add (glow), multiply, screen. Space switches the circle to “add”.

light.cap: Light changes a light source’s brightness and colour. Space makes the lamp brighter and warmer.

text.cap: Text builds a string; {value} is replaced by the incoming signal. Here the number 5 becomes “Score: 5!”.

toNumber.cap: To Number turns text into a number (or sends “invalid”). “42 coins” → 42, symbols stripped.

textCompare.cap: Text Compare tests two texts (equals, contains, starts with, regex…) and sends true or false.

numberList.cap: Number List makes a list of numbers – typed out or a range. Here 1 to 5 step 1.

listModify.cap: List Modify adds, removes, inserts or replaces items in a named list. Each Space adds “kiwi” to the fruit list.

listOrder.cap: List Order sorts, shuffles, reverses or picks a random item from a list. Here it sorts the fruit A → Z.

listEach.cap: List Each walks through a list one item at a time (every 0.5 s here) – “item” fires for each one, then “done”.

listCount.cap: List Count tells you how many items a list has (all, numbers only or unique) and whether it is empty.

label.cap: Label draws text on the screen (HUD). Use {variable} to show live values – each Space press adds 1 to the score.

bar.cap: Bar draws a progress / health bar from a variable (here “health”, max 100). Each press takes 20 off.

joystick.cap: Joystick adds an on-screen stick for phones and tablets (it holds W A S D or arrow keys). Drag it – the box follows. Move it in the UI layer.

touchButton.cap: Touch Button is an on-screen button that presses a key (here Space). Tap it and the keyboard trigger fires.

touchLook.cap: Touch Look turns a drag (or a look-stick) into camera movement – “dx / dy” show how far you dragged. In 3D it feeds the camera look.

alert.cap: Alert shows a pop-up message (toast or modal) – success, warning, error… Press Space to see it.

cursor.cap: Cursor replaces the mouse pointer with a ring, cross, emoji or your own image while playing.

pauseGame.cap: Pause Game freezes or resumes the game (toggle / pause / resume). Press P: the spinning box stops, press again to continue.

loadLevel.cap: Load Level switches to another scene (“next”, a name or a number). Press Space to go to level 2.

restartGame.cap: Restart Game starts the scene (or whole game) again. The box drifts away; Space brings everything back to the start.

fetchUrl.cap: Fetch URL loads data from the web (GET/POST) and sends the result. Space fetches a GitHub “zen” quote.

saveValue.cap: Save Value stores a value on this device (a high score…) and loads it back later. S saves 99, L loads it.

gameSave.cap: Game Save stores the whole game state in a slot and restores it. Right moves the box, S saves, L loads – the box jumps back.

leaderboard.cap: Leaderboard submits scores and shows the top list. Space submits 120 points, L shows the board.

achievement.cap: Achievement unlocks a badge once and shows a toast (“already” fires if it was earned before). Press Space.

level.cap: Level tells you about the current level: its number, name and how many there are – or marks it complete.

gamePhysics.cap: Game Physics changes the world: gravity, time scale (slow motion), debug view. Space switches gravity on – the box falls.

userInfo.cap: User Info reads facts about the player’s device: platform, language, screen size, dark mode, time zone… Space shows the platform.

clipboard.cap: Clipboard copies text to the clipboard or pastes it. C copies “Hello!”, V pastes it back into the label.

cloud.cap: Cloud saves and loads your game online with the player’s account (sign in first). Here it reports whether the player is signed in.

fullScreen.cap: Full Screen enters or leaves full-screen mode (a browser needs a click or key to allow it). Space toggles it.

shake.cap: Shake fires when the phone is shaken (on a computer press H to test). Use it for “shake to reset” or dice rolls.

ad.cap: Ad shows an interstitial, rewarded or banner ad (house ads built in; plug in your own provider). Space shows one.

vibrate.cap: Vibrate buzzes the phone (a pattern in milliseconds, e.g. 150 or 100,50,100). The flash stands in for the buzz here.

accelerometer.cap: Accelerometer reads how the phone is tilted. On a computer the arrow keys pretend to tilt it. Tilt left/right and the box rolls.

gameCenter.cap: Game Center (Apple) / Play Games (Google) sign-in, scores and achievements. On a computer it reports that it is not available.

deviceCheck.cap: Device Check asks about the device – mobile, tablet, iOS, touch, landscape, dark mode… and sends yes or no.

touchCheck.cap: Touch Check detects fingers on the screen – touching, how many, or touching this object. While held, the box turns green.

exitGame.cap: Exit Game closes the game window / app (with a goodbye message). Space asks to quit.

position.cap: Position moves an object: “set” jumps to x/y, “add” moves by an amount; with a duration it glides smoothly. Press Space to slide 200 px right.

rotation.cap: Rotation turns an object to an angle (set) or by an angle (add), optionally smoothly. Space turns the box 90°.

alpha.cap: Alpha sets how see-through an object is (0 invisible – 1 solid). Space fades the box to 25 %.

size.cap: Size changes width / height (/ depth in 3D) – set, add or multiply, instantly or smoothly. Space doubles the box.

animation.cap: Animation plays a sprite animation – or a ready-made preset like bounce or pulse that works on any object. Space starts “pulse”.

velocity.cap: Velocity sets or changes how fast an object moves (px/s). Space sends the box flying right; pressing again sets it back.

spin.cap: Spin turns an object around an axis continuously (degrees per second). Space starts a 180°/s spin.

colors.cap: Colors changes an object’s colour – set a colour, blend toward it, shift the hue or pick randomly. Space picks a random colour.

shader.cap: Shader applies a screen / object effect (grayscale, blur, glitch, wavy, pixelize…). Space turns on “wavy”.

textCase.cap: Text Case converts upper/lower/title/camel/snake case. “hello big world” becomes “HELLO BIG WORLD”.

textLength.cap: Text Length counts characters, words or lines. “The quick brown fox” has 4 words.

textSanitize.cap: Text Sanitize cleans user text: trim, collapse spaces, strip HTML, limit length. “ Hi there ” → “Hi there”.

textList.cap: Text List splits text into a list (one item per line or by a separator) and sends it plus the count.

destroyer.cap: Destroy removes an object (optionally with a burst). Press Space and the box pops.

camera.cap: Camera moves, zooms, follows or shakes the view. Press Space for a screen shake (also: follow, zoom, look-at in 3D).

message.cap: Message sends a text/value to other objects (target + channel). Here the box sends “hello”; the green Friend has a Mailbox that reacts.

rayCast.cap: Ray Cast shoots an invisible line and reports what it hits and how far. Press Space: the ray goes right, hits the wall and sends the distance.

calendar.cap: Calendar reads the real clock – date, time, weekday, hour… Here it shows the current time, refreshed every second.

clock.cap: Clock is a stopwatch, countdown or real-time clock. Here a countdown from 10 starts automatically and shows mm:ss.

bundle.cap: A Bundle packs several blocks into one reusable block. This one doubles its input: 21 goes in, 42 comes out. Double-click a bundle to open it.

bundleInput.cap: Inside a bundle, New Input creates an input socket (here “in1”) on the outside of the bundle. What arrives there comes out of this block.

bundleOutput.cap: Inside a bundle, New Output creates an output socket (here “out1”). Whatever you send into it leaves the bundle there.

microphone.cap: Microphone listens to the mic and sends the loudness (0–100) and pitch; “loud” fires above a limit. Here the level is shown live – press M to fake a loud sound.

voiceCommand.cap: Voice Command listens for spoken words (“jump”, “fire”…). Say one – or here press Space to send “jump” as if you said it.

soundDetector.cap: Sound Detector recognises claps, double claps, whistles, shouts and silence from the microphone.

voiceNoise.cap: Voice Noise turns your voice (or a test key, M) into noise other objects can hear. Press M: the red Guard hears it and walks over.

makeNoise.cap: Make Noise sends a noise out from an object (footsteps or one-off). Press M to make noise – the Guard goes to where it came from.

hearing.cap: Hearing lets an object react to noises: it faces and walks toward the source and remembers it. This Guard hears the box when M is pressed.

cameraFeed.cap: Camera Feed shows the webcam in the corner, as an overlay or behind the game (here: corner).

motionSensor.cap: Motion Sensor detects movement in the webcam image: how much, where (x, y) and swipe directions. The number rises as the picture moves.

colorTracker.cap: Color Tracker finds a colour in the webcam image and follows it (position and size). Hold a coloured object up to steer.

lightSensor.cap: Light Sensor measures how bright the webcam image is and tells you when it gets dark or bright.

faceTracker.cap: Face Tracker finds a face in the webcam image and sends its position and size (needs a browser with face detection).

photoSnap.cap: Photo Snap takes a picture from the webcam (with a flash) and stores it in a variable or downloads it. Space = click!

vrMode.cap: VR Mode adds the “Enter VR” button and switches to a headset (WebXR) or split-screen view (cardboard / computer).

vrHead.cap: VR Head follows the player’s head: position, turning (yaw/pitch/roll) and nod / shake gestures. Turn your head (here the arrow keys) and the number changes.

vrController.cap: VR Controller tracks a hand controller – trigger, grip, A / B, stick and position – and can attach an object to the hand. Here the mouse is the right hand.

vrMove.cap: VR Move walks the player around (smooth, snap-turn or teleport) with the controller stick. In the computer fallback use W A S D.

vrGrab.cap: VR Grab lets a hand pick up objects with the grip button (here anything tagged “grab”) and throw them when released.

vrHaptic.cap: VR Haptic buzzes a controller (strength + length). Press Space – on a headset your hand feels it.

vrGaze.cap: VR Gaze fires when the player looks at an object for a moment (here 1 s) – selection without controllers, ideal for cardboard viewers.

arMode.cap: AR Mode starts augmented reality: the camera behind the game (or WebXR on supported phones). Press “Start AR”.

arSurface.cap: AR Surface finds the floor / table and shows a reticle where you are pointing; it sends the hit position.

arPlace.cap: AR Place puts an object where you tap on the surface (move the object, or spawn copies). Tap the screen to place the box.

arScale.cap: AR Scale lets the player resize and turn an object with two fingers (pinch to zoom, twist to rotate).

arLight.cap: AR Light reads how bright the room is from the camera and lights the 3D objects to match.

arShadowFloor.cap: AR Shadow Floor adds an invisible floor that only shows shadows, so virtual objects look like they sit on the real surface.

arDistance.cap: AR Distance measures how far an object is from the camera (or from another object) and tells you when it is near.

coinflip.cap: Coin Flip (plugin) sends a signal out of “heads” or “tails” at random. Press Space: heads turns the box green, tails red.

clampnum.cap: Clamp Number (plugin) keeps a number between a minimum and maximum. Random 0–100 values are squeezed into 20–60.

bluetoothConnect.cap: Bluetooth Connect pairs with a Bluetooth Low Energy device – the browser shows its own picker, so start it from a key or click. Space connects (a demo band stands in here).

bluetoothRead.cap: Bluetooth Read asks a connected device for one value – here the battery level. Space connects, then reads it.

bluetoothWrite.cap: Bluetooth Write sends a value to a device (an LED, a motor…). Space connects, then writes the number 128.

bluetoothNotify.cap: Bluetooth Notify listens while the device pushes values by itself – here a heart-rate stream. Space connects and starts listening.

getField.cap: Get Field picks one value out of a signal that carries several. Size sends width + height together; Get Field “w” takes just the width (here 90).
